images.caption: The starkness of the landscape highlights the ruggedness of the terrain around the lakes in this satellite image of Band-e-Amir National Park. Towering cliffs create sharp lines and shadows on the south (bottom) side of many of the lakes. The lakes range in color from faint turquoise to deep blue.
images.alt: The starkness of the landscape highlights the ruggedness of the terrain around the lakes in this satellite image of Band-e-Amir National Park. Towering cliffs create sharp lines and shadows on the south (bottom) side of many of the lakes. The lakes range in color from faint turquoise to deep blue.
images.artist: NASA image created by Jesse Allen, using Landsat data provided by the United States Geological Survey.

images.caption: On June 18th, Ambassador Eikenberry joined Governor Sarobi, Second Vice President Karim Khalili, Director General of the National Environmental Protection Agency Mostapha Zaher, and Bamyan provincial leadership to celebrate Band-e-Amir National Park. Long known among Afghans as a place of great natural beauty and cool respite during the summer, the park opened in April for tourists.

The entrance and checkpoint of the Band-e Amir National Park, Afghanistan. The poster on the wall is the fee schedule (as of 2025):
Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan
Band-e Amir National Park Fee Schedule
1. Foreign tourists — 800 Afghanis
2. Domestic tourists — 50 Afghanis
3. Foreign tourist vehicle — 200 Afghanis
4. Domestic tourist vehicle — 50 Afghanis
5. Foreign motorcycle — 100 Afghanis
6. Domestic motorcycle — 50 Afghanis
7. Boat — 100 Afghanis
8. Paddle boat / recreational boat — 200 Afghanis
9. Foreign tourist camping/tent fee — 500 Afghanis
10. Domestic tourist camping/tent fee — 200 Afghanis

11. Commercial photography/filming — 1,000 Afghanis
